Title: Patrologiae graecae tomus CLIX: Laonicus Chalcocondyla, Josephus Methonensis, alii. Laonici Chalcocondylae Historiarum libri decem; accedunt Josephi Methonensis episcopi, Joannis Plusiadeni scripta quae exstant; praemittuntur Leonardi Chiensis Mitylenaei archiepiscopi, Isidori S.R.E. cardinalis, Ruthenorum archiepiscopi (epistolae). Tomus unicus
Creator: Laonikos Chalkokondyles (history of the Ottomans and the fall of Constantinople); Leonard of Chios, archbishop of Mytilene; Cardinal Isidore of Kiev; Joseph of Methone (Joannes Plusiadenos); Greek texts with Latin, edited by J.-P. Migne
Publisher: Paris: J.-P. Migne (Petit-Montrouge), Patrologiae cursus completus, Series graeca, tomus 159
Publication Date: 1866
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the title page's OCR reads '1860' at file line 221; the list of Migne's volumes in tomus CLXI (file line 110965 of the Bessarion volume) reads 'CLVIX (1866). Laonicus Chalcondylus, 9-922. Leonardus Chiensis, 923-44. Isidorus, cardinalis, 943-56. Josephus Methonensis (Joannes Plusiadenus), 957-1394'. Either year is far before 1930. Host record: date field 1857, volume 159, possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.
Language: grc (Greek with parallel or following Latin translation; the Latin and Greek share the OCR file; see the content note)
Source: Internet Archive item patrologicursus44migngoog (archive.org/details/patrologicursus44migngoog), full-text file patrologicursus44migngoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows it unchanged. Nothing was stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped (the long s glyph occurs 213 times and was left as found). The Google Books boilerplate page at the head of the OCR is left in place. The OCR text that follows is 4381258 bytes, 3375885 characters and 90961 lines. OCR quality sampled at the title pages and at about 5%, 50% and 95% of the file (lines 4561, 45493 and 86425): Greek polytonic readable with chi-for-kappa slips; Latin clean with ordinary slips.
Content note: Tomus 159 as its ELENCHUS lists it: Laonikos Chalkokondyles's ten books of history, with the Turkish annals added by Leunclavius; Leonard of Chios's letter to Pope Nicholas V on the capture of the City (dated 15 August 1453, from file line 54400) and Cardinal Isidore's letter to all the faithful on the fall (from 55412), both by churchmen who were in or near the City; and the works of Joseph of Methone (Joannes Plusiadenos), a Greek who supported the union: On the differences between Greeks and Latins (from 56228), the Response to Mark of Ephesus's libel, a canon on the Florentine synod and an Annexarium of what was done at Florence, with the editors' note giving the Defensio quinque capitum to him rather than to Scholarios.
